rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader mid-instruction. Present. Body-region grep (derive-body-view.js, planted_proof true) returned banned_words body_hits=1; verified at L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' The hook's SUBS table did not fire, so the word shipped verbatim.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the adverb; the sentence states the claim without it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: naming an exercise a ritual ships the Scrum-ceremony register the whole compound loop exists to replace. Present. Body grep ritual_ceremony body_hits=1, verified at L11: 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.'
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: The word is exercise, or drop the sentence — nothing above it needs a repeat instruction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: changelog in a file a student reads; history belongs in git. Present, and in body prose rather than a maintainer block, so the dated-provenance carve-out does not reach it. Body grep session_biography body_hits=1 and dated_line body_hits=1, both at L49: 'This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.' Transition verbs ('previously said', 'was fixed') fail the tense test outright.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the line; a reader who never saw the old version loses nothing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 quintet (Boris x Martin x Godin x Sutherland x Siilasmaa). Three lines sit outside it: L11 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' is SAFe-coach; L37 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' is L&D-reassurance, not peer-flat; L24 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' is trainer-narration read aloud to the student. Harm is register drift the student feels as being handled rather than addressed.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: All three are cuts, not rewrites — the surrounding prose already carries the beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L57 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM' — the backing block attributes it to the maintainer's own frame, so no practitioner credit is owed. Creator-name grep over the body region returned zero ('Antti', 'the creator', 'the author'), and the author-we grep reported body_hits=0 with planted_proof true.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: third-person teacher voice leaking into a surface the student reads, which also states delivery mechanics that belong below the fence. Present. Body grep the_student body_hits=1, verified at L24: 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' Not the Connections room-harvest carve-out — this is an exercise step, not a Connections paragraph.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut it, or move the observation to the maintainer block as a trainer note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L43 'Adding a connector is one command per tracker.' The maintainer block carries a standing accept-note at L72 ruling 'connector' assumed-known for this audience and instructing judges not to re-file it, so the term is settled, not smuggled.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: reassurance signalling the author thought the beat needed defending; a senior engineer reads it as apology. Present. L37: 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' It matches two of the rule's named flags at once ('no penalty', 'fine ... either way') and defends a push-back step L39 already frames as worth doing.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the whole sentence; L39 carries the invitation on its own.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slogan shipping without the boundary that makes it true. The backing stance at L134 defends the bare header L55 '## Anything can be reverse-engineered' by asserting the boundary 'is carried in the third bullet per check_writing.md §12' and instructs judges to 'read the third bullet before flagging'. That section has exactly two bullets (L57, L58) and neither states the promised caveat that extraction quality tracks the quality of the data sampled. The carve-out §12 requires is absent from the body, and the note that would have made a judge stop is stale (§3's keep-notes-bind clause).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either restore the boundary bullet after L58 or rewrite the stance note to describe what the section actually carries — not both silently.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No body hit on 'vendor', 'not an aspirational', 'the real practitioners', 'grounded in actual', 'not theoretical'. Closest is L30 'One the agent just wrote carries none of your team's conventions.' — a mechanical reason inside the beat, not a positioning defence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The pronoun/referent half of this rule fires on any closer, not only post-trim. L53 opens its section with 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' — 'it' has no noun anywhere in the section, and the nearest candidates upstream (L45) are three: the close-out, the ticket, and what the agent reported. Read cold at slide grain, which is how this `##` section is projected, the reader has to hunt.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the noun: 'Does the close-out sound like the comments already on the ticket?'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it
rules_evaluated.evidence: L60-L64 keeps the three moves: count plus noun ('Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note ... and the conventions ...'), one qualifier, and a destination ('The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.'). Past tense throughout, no replay of the steps. Closest to violating: it runs four sentences and about 51 words against the stated 25-40 word budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L39 'Push back on the five.' — push-back is the training's own peer-flat frame for review, not a combative verb from the banned set (bark, order, command, whip, boss). No hit on any listed verb in the body region.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L30 'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works. One the agent just wrote carries none of your team's conventions.' The negation lands on a prior the student really holds (reaching for a ticket the session just created), so it is not empty negation. No deictic drumroll and no bold-label echo in the body region.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L33 'propose five bug rules' and L39 'Push back on the five.' Neither sits above a list of five items in the body — five is what the agent is asked to produce, a count of real things, and L39 reuses it as a handle after the fence. No adjacent enumeration to duplicate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L55 '## Anything can be reverse-engineered' carries a superlative ('anything') asserted about the world, so it owes the truth test. It survives it as framing because the claim has a broad true reading and is maintainer-attested at L125; what it lacks is the boundary §12 requires, which is filed on the §12 row rather than here. Do not double-file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L53 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' The test points at an external artifact the student did not generate in this session, so it can come back negative. Not self-witnessing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L24 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' It narrates the reader from outside, which reads faintly corrective, but it names no tier and asserts no deficiency — the defect is third-person teacher framing, filed under check_writing §7. No ability-level phrasing anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L43 'connector'. The maintainer accept-note at L72 (Antti 2026-08-18) rules it assumed-known for the AE101 engineer audience and says explicitly that §2 findings on it are overruled. Every other term in the body (ticket, tracker, labels, severity, repro steps, CI pipeline) is ordinary working vocabulary for this audience.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two recoveries sit in body: L18 'If there is no ticket for this bug, say so in the chat.' and L30 'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works.' Both clear the base test — plausible failure, non-obvious rescue, one tight line — so body is the right surface; routing them below the fence would delete them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L53 'If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.' This is the register-read the rule's own exemption blesses, and per the rule's own warning about scoped exemptions I re-ran the other clauses: the object is named (the wording on the ticket), the tell is given (does it sound like the existing comments), the speech verb carries its addressee ('tell Claude'), and the move is executable. Nothing here asks for manual error-catching.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four of six headers lead with a verb (L15 'Read the ticket for your bug', L26 'Read the conventions off the ticket', L41 'Write the close-out and send it', L51 'Double-check the voice'). Closest to violating: L55 '## Anything can be reverse-engineered', declarative over a section whose second bullet asks for an action — but the section's job is the generalisation the student carries away, which the rule allows a noun-phrase header for.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L43 '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' — link text is the target's H1 title, not a filename and not a code-span path. The `../` path form is governed by curriculum/module-shape.md, not by this rule, which states so explicitly; not filed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Split is clean: acting goes to 'the agent' (L18, L29, L30, L31, L58), invocation to 'Claude' (L33, L45, L53), and the one capability claim about thinking uses 'an LLM' (L57 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM'). No Claude-count skew.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: noun-run for the agent's sitting collides with the test/CI sense the same body uses two lines later, and the corpus banned it to keep 'session' unambiguous. Present at L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Here 'the run' means this session's behaviour, which is exactly the banned noun-run; the legal senses (test/CI executions, quoted text, artifact names, 'long-running') do not cover it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: The line is already cut for §1; if any of it is kept, 'the session' is the word.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a clause that changes nothing the student understands, decides or does. L37 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' fails both screens — it makes no next sentence better, and it is obvious to any working engineer that an optional step is optional. Filed separately from check_writing §9 because the two rules cut it for different reasons; one deletion clears both.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L24 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' It carries a 'notice' verb right after a prompt fence, but the object is state in the test runner rather than the artifact the agent just printed in chat, so the rule's harm (telling the reader to do what they are already doing) is not what fires here. The line is filed under check_writing §7 instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L64 'The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' On the predicate-leak clause this reads as cartography, but check_writing §16 move 3 explicitly requires the What-happened block to land on what reads the artifact next, and the more specific rule governs. Raised as a rule question in notes rather than filed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three markers carry a lead-in under 20 words: L20 'Drop the ticket link after the colon.', L33 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs and propose five bug rules.', L45 'Ask Claude to write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote.' L20 is the §2a dangling-colon shape done right — the fence ends 'Ticket:' and the lead-in names only what to drop in.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L33 'reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs' against close-the-ticket-2's opening 'Reverse-engineer how this team handles bugs from one bug ticket' — same verb, same noun-phrase. L45 'write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote' against close-the-ticket-3's 'Update the ticket: short close-out note ... Tell me what you wrote.' — shared verb and noun, rhyme holds.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned word ships in student-facing body; consultancy register flinches the engineer reader mid-instruction.
findings.fix: Cut the adverb, or cut the sentence — the beat below already says what changes.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Hard-banned word; ships the Scrum-ceremony register the compound loop exists to replace.
findings.fix: Delete the line; nothing above it asks for a repeat instruction.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher framing in body prose; also states delivery mechanics that belong below the fence.
findings.fix: Delete, or move to the maintainer block as a trainer note.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Changelog in body prose; a reader who never saw the old version loses nothing, and the transition verbs fail the tense test.
findings.fix: Delete the line. History is git.

findings.quote: There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.
findings.harm: Reassurance-shaped sentence defending an optional step; peer voice does not apologise for pragmatism, and the clause changes nothing the student does.
findings.fix: Delete; L39 already carries the invitation.

findings.harm: Noun-run for the agent's sitting, which the corpus bans to keep session unambiguous against the CI sense.
findings.fix: 'the session' if any of the line survives the §1 cut.

findings.harm: Slogan ships without the boundary §12 requires; the backing stance tells future judges to 'read the third bullet before flagging' and the section has only two, neither carrying the promised caveat.
findings.fix: Restore the boundary bullet after L58, or rewrite the stance note to state what the section actually carries.

findings.quote: Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?
findings.harm: Opening pronoun with no noun in its section and three candidates upstream; read cold at slide grain the reader has to hunt.
findings.fix: 'Does the close-out sound like the comments already on the ticket?'

todos.note: Register: L11, L24 and L37 together pull the file toward L&D-coach; all three are cuts, not rewrites.
Backing-block stance promises a third bullet that does not exist; §3's keep-notes-bind clause makes this the note's edit surface too.
Name the close-out instead of opening the section on 'it'.
What-happened block runs four sentences and about 51 words against the stated 25-40 budget; shape is otherwise correct.
Same line as the §9 over-hedge; one deletion clears both.
